llm.summary: The visible artifacts match a research-paper subscription tool, but it stores local subscription data and creates scheduled cron jobs that users should review before enabling.

dimensions.detail: The OpenAlex querying, paper filtering, summaries, and subscription management are coherent with the stated purpose. The notable capability is recurring scheduled delivery, which is expected for this skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions include user-confirmation steps for time, timezone, journals, topics, and scheduling changes. No evidence was found that the skill asks the agent to ignore the user or override user intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec or third-party package install. The visible script uses Python standard-library modules and an optional curl fallback. The provided script artifact is marked truncated, so confidence is limited for the unseen remainder.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script makes outbound requests to https://api.openalex.org and writes local subscription JSON files. These behaviors are disclosed and aligned with the paper-monitoring purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill registers and removes cron jobs for recurring paper checks. This persistence is central to the skill, but users should verify each scheduled job and remove subscriptions they no longer want.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This appears purpose-aligned for scheduled OpenAlex paper summaries. Before installing or using it, confirm each cron schedule, recipient ID, timezone, and topic list, and do not publish or share the generated data directory. If any chat-channel credentials are required in your environment, keep them separate from the skill files.

evidence.explanation: The skill intentionally creates recurring scheduled work. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it can continue running after the initial interaction until removed.
evidence.snippet: `add` — create a subscription and register a cron job.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Create cron jobs only after the user explicitly requests a subscription, verify the scheduled time and timezone, and use the documented remove action when the subscription is no longer wanted.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A daily paper-monitoring job may keep running and sending summaries until the user cancels it.

evidence.explanation: The script persists recipient IDs, topics, journals, schedule settings, and last-checked state in a local JSON file.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Do not publish generated data files, keep the data directory local, and delete subscriptions or the JSON file when no longer needed.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Recipient IDs and research interests may remain on disk and be reused by future scheduled runs.

evidence.explanation: The script can invoke the local curl binary as a fallback when Python HTTPS access fails. The command is static, does not use a shell, and targets the OpenAlex URL built by the script.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Allow this only in environments where outbound OpenAlex access is acceptable, and review network policy if curl usage is restricted.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: The skill may make an outbound network request through curl if Python's HTTPS request fails.

evidence.explanation: The capability signal indicates possible credential-sensitive behavior, while the visible SKILL.md says OpenAlex needs no API key and the visible script only shows recipient IDs and optional OPENALEX_MAILTO.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Keep any chat or push-channel credentials outside the skill folder, use scoped credentials if needed, and verify that generated data files do not contain secrets.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: If a chat-channel push integration requires credentials outside the visible code, those credentials could be sensitive even though no token handling is shown here.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The skill creates scheduled cron jobs and can invoke curl for OpenAlex requests; both are disclosed and aligned with the subscription purpose.

permission_boundary.summary: A capability signal mentions sensitive credentials, but the visible artifacts do not show API-key or token handling.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: The skill stores local subscription data, including recipient IDs and research topics, in generated JSON files.
